text:
maria: Heads-up — overnight canary on private cluster hit KMS timeouts after we tightened netpols. Pods in namespace `keystore` failing decrypts, logs show denied egress to kms.redwood-infra.prod:443. Need quick triage before morning.

jon: Saw that too. Service is `private-keystore`. NetPol rolled yesterday (deny-all-egress + allow S3). Likely we blocked KMS egress. Can someone repro and propose mitigation?

maria: Repro steps: `kubectl exec -n keystore -it pod/keystore-0 -- curl -v https://kms.redwood-infra.prod:443/health` -> `Connection timed out`. App error: `KMS_EGRESS_TIMEOUT`. Also noticed no failed decrypt audit entry (we normally see a request id even for failures). Snippet from pod logs: 
```
2026-07-12T03:12:44Z keystore ERROR decrypt failed err=KMS_EGRESS_TIMEOUT
2026-07-12T03:12:44Z keystore DEBUG outbound egress blocked to kms.redwood-infra.prod:443 netpol=deny-all-egress-v2
```

sam: If netpol blocks the SYN, the client never opens a socket so nothing reaches KMS and no audit record is generated. Quick mitigation: add an egress rule for `kms.redwood-infra.prod:443` for namespace `keystore`. I can patch in ~10m. Example patch: 
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-kms-egress-keystore
  namespace: keystore
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          infra: controlplane
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 443
```
Apply as hotfix, then we can tighten to FQDN/IPset later. :thumbsup:

lia: Also double-check RBAC for the service account. `svc-keystore` was part of last week's least-privilege cleanup — IIRC kms perms were scoped down. If SA lacks `kms:Decrypt`, adding netpol rule won't help.

maria: Confirmed: PR#1234 removed kms decrypt permission for `svc-keystore` (intent: reduce blast radius). That combined with netpol change caused the outage. Pinging @jon to revert temporarily.

jon: I'll revert the RBAC change in PR#1234 now and push. Also creating an incident ticket so we track RCA. @sec-bot please create an incident.

sec-bot: incident created: INC-2026-045 — "Private-keystore KMS egress blocked after netpol tighten". Severity: P2. Pager notified.

sam: Netpol patch applied and RBAC revert merged. Rolling restart keystore pods. Initial logs: 
```
2026-07-12T03:21:03Z keystore INFO connected to kms host=kms.redwood-infra.prod request_id=abcd-1234 status=200
2026-07-12T03:21:03Z keystore INFO decrypt succeeded request_id=abcd-1234 principal=svc-keystore
```

maria: Verified audit logs now show the decrypt attempts with request ids. Good recovery. Follow-ups: add e2e test in staging that verifies keystore -> KMS egress after netpol changes. Owners: netpol (sam), RBAC (jon), audit checks (maria).

lia: Postmortem action items (I'll open tickets): 1) e2e test for keystore KMS path, 2) alert: if keystore pods have >10% failed egress to KMS for 5m, page SRE, 3) canonical netpol template for keystore with documented allowed FQDNs/IP sets, 4) gate for RBAC PRs touching `svc-keystore` to require sign-off from security.

maria: Thanks all. Quick operational note — keep deny-all as default, but we should maintain a small allowlist for core infra (KMS, STS, metadata endpoints) and a documented process for adding entries. Also let's surface netpol denials in cluster logs (reason + flow) to make future triage faster. :eyes:
